item.title: 'Happy 55th birthday': UN officials reaffirm stance on China's UN seat
item.description: Senior United Nations officials have reaffirmed the world body's unwavering adherence to UN General Assembly (UNGA) Resolution 2758, as Sunday marks the 55th anniversary of the restoration of China's lawful seat at the UN.
item.content:encoded:
Senior United Nations officials have reaffirmed the world body's unwavering adherence to UN General Assembly (UNGA) Resolution 2758, as Sunday marks the 55th anniversary of the restoration of China's lawful seat at the UN.

Speaking to CGTN on the sidelines of the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan), Guy Ryder, UN under-secretary-general for policy, said the organization "continues to be guided by that resolution."

"The United Nations upholds that resolution and will do so consistently," Ryder said.

Stephen Jackson, UN resident coordinator in China, said the UN remains "firmly adherent" to the will of the General Assembly.

"Happy 55th birthday," Jackson said of the ties between the UN and China during an interview with CGTN.

Fifty-five years ago, on October 25, 1971, the UNGA adopted Resolution 2758 at its 26th session with an overwhelming majority, deciding to restore all rights of the People's Republic of China in the United Nations. From the perspective of international law, this resolution completely eliminated possibilities of "two Chinas" or "Taiwan independence."

"That was a historic moment," Jackson said. "It brought the United Nations into line with a political and historical reality."

Equally important, the resolution brought to the table, including in one of the UN's highest bodies, the Security Council, "a powerful voice" from the Global South with China's seat restored, he stressed.

The adoption of the resolution was "a really determinant moment" not only for China, but also for the United Nations, Jackson said.

The relationship between China and the UN has remained "very, very" close over the past 55 years, he added.

The UN official expressed confidence that the incoming secretary-general – whoever is ultimately selected through the ongoing voting process – will carry forward a China-UN relationship that remains "both central and strong."

Commenting on the restoration of China's lawful UN seat in 1971, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Friday that it marked the return of the Chinese people, one-fourth of the world's population, to the UN stage.

Through the UN, China works to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with other countries, advocate for common security, promote shared development, foster dialogue among civilizations and advance the reform and improvement of global governance, Mao said.

item.title: China's top diplomat holds talks with FM of Republic of the Congo
item.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held talks with Constant-Serge Bounda, minister of foreign affairs, La Francophonie and Congolese Abroad of the Republic of the Congo, on Thursday in Beijing.
item.content:encoded:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held talks with Constant-Serge Bounda, minister of foreign affairs, La Francophonie and Congolese Abroad of the Republic of the Congo, on Thursday in Beijing.

Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said the Republic of the Congo is the first African country to join China in signing the Early Harvest Arrangement for the Agreement on Economic Partnership for Shared Development.

China will continue to support the Republic of the Congo in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions and opposing all forms of bullying by external forces, Wang said.

Wang said China stands ready, under the strategic guidance of the two countries' heads of state, to work with the Republic of the Congo to plan high-level exchanges for the next stage, strengthen strategic alignment, advance practical cooperation and promote bilateral ties.

Calling on both sides to make full preparations for the Tenth Ministerial Conference of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, scheduled to be held in the Republic of the Congo in 2027, Wang said China is ready to work with African parties to build a more just and equitable global governance system that meets the shared aspirations of Global South countries.

The two sides should make good use of multilateral platforms, including the International Organization for Mediation and the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, and step up communication and coordination, Wang added.

Bounda said the Republic of the Congo supports the series of global initiatives put forward by China and reaffirms its firm commitment to the one-China principle.

The Republic of the Congo appreciates China's attention to Africa's health sector and its assistance to Africa in combating the Ebola epidemic and strengthening health infrastructure development, Bounda said, noting that it stands ready to work with China to jointly advance Africa-China relations.

item.title: Chinese medical team brings free TCM care to Sierra Leone
item.description: The 27th Chinese medical team to Sierra Leone has conducted a series of free community health clinics across the capital region this month, delivering specialized pain management, general care and medical training to local residents.
item.content:encoded:
The 27th Chinese medical team to Sierra Leone has conducted a series of free community health clinics across the capital region this month, delivering specialized pain management, general care and medical training to local residents.

The medical outreach, organized by the Traditional Chinese Medicine Center at the Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital under China's "100 Medical Teams in 1,000 Villages" program, included a special TCM session at the Calaba Town Health Center to mark Thursday's 35th World Traditional Medicine Day.

Targeting widespread chronic conditions caused by heavy physical labor, Chinese specialists and local staff served nearly 100 residents in Calaba Town. Doctors used specialized therapies – including Fu's Subcutaneous Needling, balance acupuncture, tuina massage and scraping – providing immediate relief for chronic neck, shoulder and joint pain.

Earlier this month, the team also provided multi-specialty screenings in the western suburbs, including blood pressure and glucose checks, general consultations and cataract screenings for future free surgeries. Besides treatments, specialists offered health education, taught therapeutic exercise routines and delivered hands-on clinical training to local doctors using real cases.

Mohamed K. Fabba, head of the Calaba Town Health Center, commended the initiative for addressing pressing community healthcare needs and expressed hope for expanded cooperation.

The medical team confirmed plans to broaden grassroots services and clinical training across the country under the China-Africa Health Partnership Initiative.

(With input from agencies)

item.title: COMESA leaders call for stronger regional trade and integration
item.description: COMESA leaders have called for stronger regional integration, increased intra-African trade and greater local processing of natural resources to accelerate economic growth and industrialization. At the bloc's 25th summit in Zimbabwe, new chairperson Emmerson Mnangagwa and outgoing chairperson William Ruto urged member states to address trade barriers, strengthen regional value chains and improve cooperation to boost Africa's competitiveness.
item.content:encoded:
Leaders from the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) have called for stronger regional integration and increased intra-African trade to drive economic growth and industrialization.

The call was made Thursday at the bloc's 25th Heads of State and Government Summit in Mount Hampden, outside Zimbabwe's capital, Harare, where Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa took over as COMESA chairperson from Kenyan President William Ruto.

Mnangagwa urged the bloc's 21 member states to harness their resources and investment potential to accelerate industrialization and expand cross-border trade.

He called for measures to address non-tariff barriers, infrastructure gaps and differences in national policies, including simpler border procedures, digital trade systems and innovative financing for infrastructure development.

He also urged countries to process more of their natural resources locally to create jobs and promote sustainable economic growth.

Outgoing chairperson Ruto said stronger regional integration was increasingly important amid rising geopolitical tensions, protectionism and disruptions to global supply chains.

He urged African countries to expand intra-African trade, develop resilient regional value chains and reduce reliance on exporting raw materials without adding value.

Ruto said COMESA could strengthen Africa's position in global trade by enabling member states to negotiate as a unified market.

He also stressed the importance of peace, security and good governance, calling for stronger regional capacity to prevent conflict.

COMESA brings together 21 member states and seeks to promote regional economic integration through trade, investment and infrastructure development.

item.title: Completion ceremony held for renovated CPV martyrs' cemetery in DPRK
item.description: A completion ceremony for the renovation project for Chinese People's Volunteers (CPV) martyrs' cemeteries was held Saturday in Sinphyong County, North Hwanghae Province of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), on the occasion of the 76th anniversary of the CPV's entry into the DPRK to fight in the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea.
item.content:encoded:
A completion ceremony for the renovation project for Chinese People's Volunteers (CPV) martyrs' cemeteries was held Saturday in Sinphyong County, North Hwanghae Province of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), on the occasion of the 76th anniversary of the CPV's entry into the DPRK to fight in the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea.

The ceremony started at around 10 a.m. (0100 GMT) with the national anthems of China and the DPRK. Representatives from China and the DPRK laid flower baskets for the CPV martyrs, stood in silent tribute, presented flowers and poured liquor in remembrance, and visited the martyrs' tombs and the wall of martyrs' names to pay profound respect.

Qi Han, charge d'affaires ad interim of the Chinese Embassy in the DPRK, said that 76 years ago, the CPV fought shoulder to shoulder with the DPRK army and people, shared weal and woe, and the traditional China-DPRK friendship forged in blood will never fade.

China stands ready to continue to work with the DPRK to implement the important consensus reached by the top leaders of the two parties and the two countries, do well in honoring and commemorating the CPV martyrs in the DPRK, consolidate traditional bonds of ties, enhance strategic coordination, maintain regional peace, honor the martyrs who sacrificed their lives and benefit the two peoples via peace and development, Qi said.

Hong Zongming, vice minister of China's Ministry of Veterans Affairs, said the memorial facilities for the CPV martyrs in the DPRK are "an important platform" for carrying forward the spirit of the fallen heroes and the China-DPRK friendship.

Calling the protection and management of the memorial facilities "a lofty cause passed down from generation to generation," Kang Chol Ho, vice minister of the Ministry of Urban Management of the DPRK, said the undertaking is dedicated to carrying forward the great spirit of the CPV fighters demonstrated in the war.

The DPRK side will work with the Chinese side to continue doing relevant work well and make positive contributions to inheriting and promoting the traditional friendship, he said.

In late October 2025, China and the DPRK held a groundbreaking ceremony in Sinphyong County for the renovation project. As of this month, the renovation has been completed at five CPV martyrs' cemeteries in the DPRK, through joint efforts by relevant Chinese and DPRK departments and agencies.

(Cover: A completion ceremony for the renovation project for Chinese People's Volunteers martyrs' cemeteries is held in Sinphyong County, North Hwanghae Province, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, October 24, 2026. /CMG )

item.title: Anthropic files for IPO, reveals soaring revenue, massive net losses
item.description: US AI company Anthropic publicly filed its prospectus for an initial public offering (IPO) on Monday, which could become the largest stock market debut in history.
item.content:encoded:
US artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic publicly filed its prospectus for an initial public offering (IPO) on Monday, which could become the largest stock market debut in history.

The filing, a registration statement on Form S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, did not set the number of shares to be sold or a price range. Anthropic intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT, according to a release on the company's website.

Both the company and existing shareholders will sell shares, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley named first among 24 underwriters. The company is expected to begin trading in mid-November, and backers hope for a valuation of up to $2 trillion, though some investors have weighed a figure closer to $1.5 trillion, according to Reuters.

The prospectus offers the first detailed look at the finances of the developer of the Claude AI models. Revenues reached $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.16 billion year on year, after growing from $41 million in 2023 to $386 million in 2024 and $4.59 billion in 2025. Revenues in the second quarter alone were $11.56 billion, and the company reported its first quarterly operating profit of $974 million.

The headline losses are far larger, but most stem from accounting charges rather than cash spending. Anthropic recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, of which $72.4 billion came from changes in the fair value of convertible notes and other instruments as the company's own valuation climbed. Its operating loss for the period was $693 million, while operating cash flow turned positive at $3.93 billion. Cash and short-term investments totaled $131.7 billion at June 30.

The filing warns that this rapid pace may not last. "We cannot assure you [revenue] will continue to grow at all," the company said in the prospectus, which also notes it is on track for a second consecutive quarter of adjusted operating profit.

Spending on computing power remains the central cost. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing resources and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, and has committed to $518 billion in future infrastructure spending. It has agreed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon through April 2036 and at least $114.5 billion with Google through July 2033. Amazon holds $6.2 billion of notes that convert into non-voting stock, capped at 12% of the company.

By September 30, more than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million each in trailing annual revenue, and more than 11,900 generated at least $100,000, up from 950 a year earlier. Existing customers spend roughly nine times what they did a year ago, but two unnamed customers accounted for about 23% of revenues in the first half of 2026.

Public investors will be able to buy the shares but will not steer the company. A single Class F share held by the seven co-founders carries 50.1% of every stockholder vote, and a trust will elect a majority of the board. A Public Benefit Fund will hold 5% of the company in non-voting shares, and each co-founder has pledged to give 80% of their personal Anthropic equity to philanthropic causes.

The prospectus devotes sections to risk factors, including warnings that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" and that liability from extreme harm could exceed what any insurer can cover.

Anthropic raised $65 billion in May at a $965-billion valuation. A debut above $2 trillion would surpass SpaceX's $1.77-trillion listing in June, the current record. Reuters has reported Anthropic's third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion and forward projections pointing to revenue of about $190 billion to $200 billion in 2028.

item.title: Steinmeier's China visit to deepen bilateral ties on shared interests
item.description: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's visit to China highlights the importance of dialogue, mutual trust and shared economic interests in advancing bilateral ties. Stronger China-Germany engagement can also help manage differences and bring greater stability to China-EU relations.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly eight years after his last visit, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier will return to China on Tuesday for a six-day state visit.

According to the German presidency, Steinmeier will begin his trip in east China's Anhui Province, visiting a traditional village to learn about the country's rural history and Volkswagen China Technology Company in Hefei. He will then travel to Beijing for formal talks at the Great Hall of the People and meet students at Peking University.

China's Foreign Ministry said Beijing hopes to use the visit to consolidate mutual trust, deepen cooperation and pursue joint innovation, advancing bilateral relations and contributing to the steady development of China-Europe ties.

Dialogue and cooperation: Building on shared interests

Volkswagen's presence in Hefei offers a concrete example of how China-Germany cooperation is evolving. The city hosts the automaker's largest global software research and development center for intelligent connected vehicles outside its headquarters in Wolfsburg, Germany, reflecting the role of China's innovation ecosystem in the company's global development.

The economic links between the two countries have long been visible in everyday business. Speaking at the Hamburg Summit in November 2016, when he was Germany's foreign minister, Steinmeier noted that nearly one in three containers unloaded at the Port of Hamburg came from China, while one in five Airbus aircraft assembled at Hamburg's Finkenwerder facility went to Chinese buyers. He cited these examples to illustrate the depth of bilateral economic ties and emphasized the importance of reliability and open dialogue in addressing differences and sustaining cooperation.

A decade later, the relationship remains substantial. According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office, bilateral trade in goods reached 251.8 billion euros ($296.6 billion) in 2025, up 2.1% year on year, making China Germany's largest trading partner once again.

Recent comments from the German business community also point to the value of maintaining this engagement. Oliver Oehms, executive director and board member of the German Chamber of Commerce in China – North China, noted that knowledge developed by German companies in China can flow back to their headquarters and strengthen their competitiveness. The chamber has called for policies that weigh benefits and risks and target specific sectors rather than impose blanket tariffs or general restrictions.

Business sentiment provides further context. A May 2026 survey by the German Chamber of Commerce in China found that 61% of surveyed German companies planned to increase investment in China over the following two years, the highest proportion since 2023. The findings suggest that many German businesses continue to see opportunities in China, underscoring the importance of a stable and predictable environment for cooperation.

German media have also highlighted the significance of Steinmeier's visit. In its October 25 coverage, Süddeutsche Zeitung described the bilateral relationship as multifaceted but complex, with trade ties undergoing adjustment. The visit comes as both countries seek to shape the next stage of their relationship through continued engagement.

China, for its part, has emphasized continuity in its approach to Germany. Announcing the visit on October 23, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said mutual respect and mutual trust had underpinned bilateral relations for 54 years, while mutual benefit remained key to successful cooperation. She said China hoped to use the visit to consolidate trust, deepen cooperation and pursue joint innovation.

Beyond bilateral ties: A stabilizing force for China-Europe relations

Besides advancing bilateral ties, Steinmeier's visit has an explicit European dimension. Euronews' German-language service reported that his office presented the trip as a visit undertaken both as Germany's head of state and as a European, following consultations with EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic and close coordination with Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

As Europe's largest economy and a key member of the European Union, Germany plays an important role in shaping the bloc's relations with China. Issues on the table in Beijing – from industrial cooperation to market access – also feature prominently in Europe's engagement with China, giving the talks relevance beyond the two countries.

The case for sustained engagement also extends beyond trade. In a 2024 research paper, Nadine Godehardt, a senior associate at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs, argued that Germany should intensify dialogue with China on security and the international order. She also identified possible EU-China initiatives on technology, infrastructure and security as avenues worth exploring.

Together, these perspectives highlight how constructive China-Germany relations can contribute to greater stability in China-Europe ties. Mutual respect and trust provide the basis for addressing differences, while open cooperation gives both sides a shared interest in finding workable solutions. By keeping dialogue active and translating common interests into practical progress, Beijing and Berlin can help prevent individual disputes from dominating the wider agenda and strengthen the strategic stability of China-EU relations.

item.title: 4 killed in southern Philippines ambush
item.description: 4 killed in southern Philippines ambush
item.content:encoded:
Four people were killed in an ambush in Maguindanao del Sur in the southern Philippines at 3 p.m. on Monday, local police said.

The vehicle carrying the victims crashed into a roadside ditch during the attack. The car came under gunfire, and the victims sustained gunshot wounds to various parts of their bodies, according to police.

The victims have not yet been identified, and investigations are underway.

item.content:encoded: China has extended deep condolences over the passing of former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday that Fukuda long championed China-Japan friendship and upheld a correct view of history.

item.title: China hopes India will work in same direction to maintain border peace
item.description: China strictly abides by relevant agreements and common understandings reached with India and conducts routine border patrols and control activities to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maintain stability in border areas, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
China strictly abides by relevant agreements and common understandings reached with India and conducts routine border patrols and control activities to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maintain stability in border areas, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday.

Guo made the remarks at a regular news briefing in response to a question about Indian allegations that Chinese forces had disturbed the peace along the border.

China and India maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels, Guo said, expressing hope that India will work with China in the same direction to jointly implement the common understandings reached between the two sides and maintain peace and tranquility in border areas through concrete actions.

item.title: Nepal plans flood warnings, glacial lake risk reduction
item.description: Nepal plans flood warnings, glacial lake risk reduction
item.content:encoded:
The Nepali government has unveiled plans to expand flood early warning systems across six major river basins and lower water levels in four high-risk glacial lakes as part of efforts to strengthen disaster preparedness amid growing climate-related risks in the Himalayan region.

The initiatives are part of a broader strategy to improve flood forecasting, reduce the risk of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) and modernize weather forecasting through advanced technologies, according to separate documents issued by the Center for Hydrology and Water Resources Research and the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, the secretariat of Nepal's Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation said in a press statement on Sunday.

The plans come in the wake of devastating floods on August 26 that claimed around 1,500 lives while more than 5,000 people remain missing. The floods also caused $1.81 billion in physical damage, according to the Nepali government's preliminary Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment (RDNA).

Rising temperatures have accelerated glacier melting in the Himalayas, increasing concerns over glacial lake instability, avalanches and potentially destructive floods downstream.

Under the proposed Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) Sanjeevani Project, the government plans to lower water levels in four high-risk glacial lakes: Thulagi in Manang district, Lower Barun in Sankhuwasabha district, and Lumding Tsho and Hongu-2 in Solukhumbu district.

The project is scheduled to run from 2026 to 2033, with an estimated budget of $49.9 million.

The initiative builds on previous efforts to reduce risks at Tsho Rolpa in Dolakha district and Imja Lake in Solukhumbu district, where water levels were successfully lowered to mitigate the threat of glacial lake outburst floods.

Meanwhile, the Center for Hydrology and Water Resources Research plans to install flood early warning systems across six river basins under the Priority River Basins Flood Risk Management Project, which runs from 2022 to 2028, with an investment of $7.54 million.

The center will also provide round-the-clock flood forecasting and early warning services from mid-May to mid-October, covering the country's main monsoon season.

In a separate initiative to improve weather forecasting, the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology plans to prioritize artificial intelligence, machine learning and high-performance computing systems to enhance the accuracy and reliability of forecasts.

item.title: Colombia seizes 3.5 tons of cocaine, arrests five in drug operation
item.description: Colombia seizes 3.5 tons of cocaine, arrests five in drug operation
item.content:encoded:
Colombia's Navy announced it seized 3.5 tons of cocaine hydrochloride in a go-fast vessel in Caribbean waters on Saturday, Oct. 17. The operation, conducted alongside the air force, also arrested five Colombian nationals in the bust. Police believe the seizure put a $170 million dent in drug trafficking organizations.

The arrested individuals, the cocaine and the boat were transferred to Cartagena, Colombia, and handed over to judicial authorities.

For more, check out our exclusive content on CGTN Now and subscribe to our weekly newsletter, The China Report.

item.title: Meet the APEC economies: Mexico
item.description: Meet the APEC economies: Mexico
item.content:encoded:
From auto parts to finished cars, Mexico's manufacturing industry is closely linked to the Asia-Pacific. 

The US, Canada, China, Japan and South Korea are among Mexico's major trading partners – all APEC economies. 

A member since 1993, Mexico is part of the regional supply chains that span the Pacific.

item.title: Meet the APEC economies: New Zealand
item.description: Meet the APEC economies: New Zealand
item.content:encoded:
From milk powder to kiwifruit, New Zealand's exports travel across the Asia-Pacific. 

More than 70% of the country's exports go to fellow APEC economies, according to the New Zealand government. 

China, Australia and the US were its three largest goods export markets in 2025, WTO data shows. 

(All photos via VCG)

item.title: Baoji Marathon draws 31,000 runners, highlights ancient culture
item.description: From race shirts to finisher medals, the 2026 Baoji Marathon in northwest China's Shaanxi Province brings Baoji's history and culture onto the course.
item.content:encoded:
From race shirts to finisher medals, the 2026 Baoji Marathon in northwest China's Shaanxi Province brings Baoji's history and culture onto the course.

The event brings together 31,000 runners, with race shirts inspired by ancient Chinese bronzeware and finisher medals modeled after the Lai Pan, a Western Zhou bronze ritual vessel. Female runners who finish in under 3 hours and 30 minutes also receive a special "Baoma" clay horse, inspired by Fengxiang clay sculpture, a national intangible cultural heritage.

Join CGTN's Merna Al Nasser for a closer look at the cultural stories behind the race designs. What's the most distinctive marathon design you've ever seen? Tell us in the comments!

item.title: China opposes US proposal to expand outbound investment curbs
item.description: China on Saturday expressed "grave concern" and "firm opposition" to a recent US Treasury proposal that would expand and intensify restrictions on outbound investment in China, calling it a discriminatory move and a typical practice of overstretching the concept of national security.
item.content:encoded:
China on Saturday expressed "grave concern" and "firm opposition" to a recent US Treasury proposal that would expand and intensify restrictions on outbound investment in China, calling it a discriminatory move and a typical practice of overstretching the concept of national security.

A spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce made the remarks in reply to a media query on the US Treasury's proposed updates to the outbound investment security program, which are open for public comment.

The proposed rules "run counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, disrupt normal economic and trade cooperation between Chinese and US enterprises, and undermine the international economic and trade order," the spokesperson said.

China will closely follow further developments and reserve the right to take corresponding measures, the spokesperson noted.

"US restrictions on investment in China would not only harm China-US economic and trade cooperation but also hurt the interests of US firms," the spokesperson said, noting that investing in China is investing in the future as the country boasts immense consumption and investment potential with its super-large market.

China urges the US side to respect market economy principles, stop overstretching the concept of national security, stop politicizing and weaponizing economic and trade issues, and create a sound environment for bilateral economic and trade cooperation, according to the spokesperson.

item.title: China's Global Governance Initiative will bolster Global South's voice
item.description: China's Global Governance Initiative will bolster Global South's voice
item.content:encoded:
The Global Governance Initiative is important not only for sharing China's experience, but also for increasing the voice of the Global South in global governance, said Annah Zhu, associate professor at Wageningen University and Research, during the 2026 Global Governance Forum in Xiongan, Hebei Province.

Zhu noted that the initiative covers governance overall, with environmental governance being a particularly important component. She added that China is currently doing more than any other country in renewable energy tree planting and greening, and that its leadership in global governance can be seen through these environmental actions.

item.title: From Karakoram to Arabian Sea, Ep. 1: The Road That Connects
item.description: From Karakoram to Arabian Sea, Ep. 1: The Road That Connects
item.content:encoded:
From the towering Karakoram mountains in the north to the shores of the Arabian Sea in the south, join CGTN’s Danial Khan on a 12-part journey across Pakistan, following the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC). Along the way, the series explores the infrastructure, industries and communities at the heart of Pakistan’s development and the growing cooperation between China and Pakistan.

Beginning at the Khunjerab Pass, where China and Pakistan meet, this episode follows the Karakoram Highway south through some of the world’s most challenging terrains. From cross-border trade at Sost Dry Port to Hunza’s rich history and the daily lives of its communities, the journey explores how this vital link between China and Pakistan is connecting people, creating opportunities and bringing new momentum to northern Pakistan.

item.title: Ethiopia-Eritrea Standoff: What’s at stake for the region?
item.description: The deep-seated standoff between Ethiopia and Eritrea revolves around fundamental questions of regional coexistence, state sovereignty, and maritime access. While the two nations briefly reconciled in 2018, the current geopolitical climate has sharply deteriorated, exposing deep fractures that threaten to destabilize the entire Horn of Africa.
item.content:encoded:
Editor’s Note: Talk Africa is a weekly talk show that brings together guests from across Africa and beyond to discuss pressing African issues and global topics, amplifying the continent's voice and showcasing diverse perspectives and independent thinking. This episode invites both Ethiopian and Eritrean guests to present their opposing views on the current standoff and discuss the possible solutions to prevent a wider regional conflict.

The deep-seated standoff between Ethiopia and Eritrea revolves around fundamental questions of regional coexistence, state sovereignty, and maritime access. While the two nations briefly reconciled in 2018, the current geopolitical climate has sharply deteriorated, exposing deep fractures that threaten to destabilize the entire Horn of Africa.

Recent border troop deployments have heightened fears of direct confrontation. Tensions escalated dramatically following the severance of diplomatic relations in early October, when Addis Ababa abruptly closed its embassy in Asmara and declared ten Eritrean diplomats persona non grata, officially accusing them of national security threats and espionage.

Sovereignty vs. Access: The Maritime Imperative

The core of the geopolitical friction is a mismatch between Ethiopia’s economic needs and Eritrea's security concerns. Following the devastating 1998–2000 border war, a brief rapprochement under Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed led to a military alliance against the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) during the 2020–2022 war. 

However, this wartime coalition quickly fractured.

“The underlying issues that confront both countries are the ability to coexist, cooperate, and also have mutual respect for each other’s sovereignty,” former UN diplomat and Horn of Africa analyst Girmay Haile, asserted. 

However, Eritrea firmly rejects any maritime cooperation that compromises its territorial sovereignty. 

Its Minister of Information, Yemane Gebremeskel, explicitly accused Ethiopia of “manufacturing crises to plot the forced annexation of the sovereign Eritrean port of Assab.”

Countering this view, Dr. Bizuneh Yimenu, an Ethiopian scholar who teaches comparative politics at Queen's University Belfast, argued that direct, reliable access to the Red Sea is an existential necessity for a landlocked nation of 140 million people.

Dr. Yimenu noted that Addis Ababa cannot wholly rely on the Djibouti corridor for 95% of its trade, leaving the nation structurally vulnerable. 

However, he maintained that maritime access is not mutually exclusive with Eritrean independence.

“This strategy explores diplomatic compromises such as free economic zones, long-term port leases, and equity-sharing mechanisms in premier state enterprises, including Ethiopian Airlines," he explained. 

Historical Scars and Border Security

Beneath the current standoff lies a profound dispute over history, troop presence, and border legitimacy, recently exacerbated by an outbreak of domestic fighting.

On September 23, 2026, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) launched a fresh armed rebellion. Though federal authority was quickly restored after Ethiopian forces recaptured Tigray’s regional capital, Mekelle, on October 9, 2026, the fallout triggered an exchange of intense cross-border accusations.

Dr. Yimenu placed the blame on Asmara’s regional posturing, asserting, “Eritrea should pull out all of its soldiers from Ethiopia and stop supporting all rebel groups operating inside Ethiopia.” 

This aligns with official claims from Ethiopia’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Gedion Timothewos, who accused Eritrea of launching an "all-out invasion," advancing 60 kilometers into northern Tigray, and colluding with internal insurgents.

Conversely, Haile rejected this narrative, countering that Eritrean troops are merely deployed in sovereign territories legally awarded to the country by the UN-backed Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission (EEBC) adjudications.

He cautioned against misleading historical revisionism, clarifying that “when Eritrea won its liberation war... It went to a UN-sponsored referendum. So the legitimacy of Eritrea to acquire its statehood is something that has been established by law.” 

Concurrently, in an appeal to the UN Security Council, Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh denied the cross-border incursion claims, accusing Addis Ababa of fabricating reports as a pretext for war while violating Eritrean airspace with hostile drone strikes.

Broken Alliance and Proxy Risks

The rapid deterioration of bilateral relations also stems from structural flaws in past diplomatic efforts and shifting geopolitical alignments. 

“Even if reconciliation happened in 2018, that reconciliation was between the two leaders. It was not institutionalized,” Dr. Yimenu noted, referring to the fragile Abiy-Afwerki rapprochement.

In his assessment, Dr. Hassan Khannenje, Director of the HORN International Institute for Strategic Studies, characterizes the current standoff as “the worst in many years.” 

He observed: “Failure to include Eritrea in the 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement planted the seeds of the current hostilities.”

These tensions have been amplified by wider regional fragmentation. Spurred by opposition to Ethiopia's controversial maritime deal with Somaliland, the leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan, and Somalia adopted the El Alamein Joint Declaration on October 4. This pact affirmed that Red Sea governance is the exclusive responsibility of its coastal states, effectively sidelining landlocked Ethiopia.

Dr. Khannenje warned that the Horn of Africa is rapidly becoming a fertile ground for proxy warfare, given its proximity to the heavily contested Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and Middle Eastern instability.

Rewriting the Rules of Engagement

While commercial frameworks like joint free trade zones theoretically offer a middle ground, the current escalatory trajectory renders their implementation highly improbable without external mediation, according to Dr. Khannenje, who laments that traditional bodies like the African Union have taken a back seat.

This diplomatic vacuum was on full display when both nations took their grievances to the UN Security Council on October 13, 2026. While UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the path to tactical de-escalation remains structurally deadlocked.

Whereas Addis Ababa places the entire burden of de-escalation on Eritrea, accusing it of acting as an aggressive regional proxy, Asmara maintains it is defending against an unprovoked war of aggression. With both sides dug into irreconcilable positions and troops actively massing on the border, the risk of a full-blown conflict remains dangerously high.

item.title: Clashes in southern Ethiopia kill nine, force 2,500 to flee to Kenya
item.description: A hospital official on the Ethiopian side of Moyale told Reuters that about 30 injured people had been admitted over several days, many with injuries caused by heavy weapons. Four died on Thursday and another five on Friday, the official said.
item.content:encoded:
At least nine people have been killed in clashes between Oromo and Somali groups in the southern Ethiopian border town of Moyale, forcing at least 2,500 people to flee across the border into neighboring Kenya, according to local hospital and Kenyan government officials.

The fighting broke out on Wednesday and continued into Friday, with residents reporting sustained gunfire. 

A hospital official on the Ethiopian side of Moyale told Reuters that about 30 injured people had been admitted over several days, many with injuries caused by heavy weapons. Four died on Thursday and another five on Friday, the official said.

Images verified by Reuters showed a bulldozer burning near a petrol station and people overturning fuel-dispensing equipment. 

The violence has also affected people on the Kenyan side. A police report said a Kenyan woman was struck in the neck by a stray bullet. The bullet was removed at a private hospital, and she was reported to be in stable condition. Kenya Red Cross said it had begun providing emergency aid to displaced families, initially targeting 1,000 households.

 

(With input from wires)

item.title: South Africa investigates outbreaks linked to poor water quality
item.description: South African authorities are investigating two separate outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness, one linked to contaminated municipal water in Tshwane and another affecting students at Rhodes University in the Eastern Cape.
item.content:encoded:
South African authorities are investigating two separate outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness, one linked to contaminated municipal water in Tshwane and another affecting students at Rhodes University in the Eastern Cape.

In Tshwane, 408 cases have been recorded in an outbreak linked to contaminated water supplied by the Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Works. Separately, Rhodes University has reported more than 100 cases among students in Makhanda, where the cause of the illnesses remains under investigation.

Officials said laboratory tests had found extremely high levels of E. coli and other bacteria in water from the treatment plant and nearby reservoirs.

Tests on stool samples from patients also detected norovirus, Campylobacter and Shigella in three of the four specimens analyzed. No cholera bacteria were found in the samples, the statement said.

An investigation by the Department of Water and Sanitation found that problems with the city’s chlorine supplier had left water from the treatment plant unchlorinated between late September and mid-October.

The investigation also found that the municipality had failed to alert residents that the water had not been chlorinated and was unsafe for human use.

The treatment plant draws water from the Bronkhorstspruit River, which the investigation found was affected by sewage pollution from dysfunctional wastewater treatment works upstream and faulty sewage pumping stations in Tshwane.

Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina said the Water Research Commission had been appointed to conduct independent water-quality tests and investigate the causes of the contamination. Its report is expected by the end of October.

President Cyril Ramaphosa apologized to affected residents on Tuesday, saying the government had intervened to address the crisis.

“We are very sorry that it has resulted in the challenge of gastrointestinal illness that has affected a number of people,” he said during a visit to Daveyton, east of Johannesburg.

Ramaphosa said the government had established a National Water Crisis Committee to coordinate the response and restore access to safe drinking water.

At Rhodes University, officials are working with local public health authorities and environmental health practitioners to determine what caused the illnesses reported among students.

The university said medical practitioners had also reported similar cases elsewhere in Makhanda, raising the possibility that the outbreak extended beyond the campus.

“While investigations are ongoing, precautionary measures have been implemented on campus, including urgent water-quality testing at residences, the provision of safe drinking water in dining halls, and additional precautions in food preparation,” the university said in a statement.

It advised staff and students to drink boiled and cooled or bottled water, use safe water to prepare food and brush their teeth, avoid ice and uncooked food washed in untreated water, and wash their hands regularly with soap and water.

In Tshwane, residents supplied by the Bronkhorstspruit system have been told not to use tap water for drinking, cooking, bathing, brushing their teeth or washing food. The water may be used only for flushing toilets until authorities confirm it is safe.

The municipality is distributing drinking water by tanker as technical teams work to address the contamination. Authorities have not announced when tap water will be safe for consumption again.

item.title: Global South 'needs to be heard,' says African official
item.description: China has built collaborative platforms for its fellow Global South members to collectively address imbalances in the global governance system, according to an African official.
item.content:encoded:
China has built collaborative platforms for its fellow Global South members to collectively address imbalances in the global governance system, according to an African official.

"The Global South doesn't need to be represented. The Global South needs to be heard," Joseph Olivier Mendo'o, executive director of the international exchange department of the China-Africa Business Council, told CGTN on the sidelines of the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan).

China, through its proposed Global Governance Initiative (GGI) that promotes the building of a more just and equitable global governance system and a better world, has been a key part of such efforts, according to Mendo'o.

Themed "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World," the three-day forum opened in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province, on Friday.

China has built collaborative platforms like the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation and supported the African Union to join the G20 to amplify the Global South's voice, he said. "China has been doing a very great job in actually setting those platforms."

Delivering a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the forum on Friday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that it is important to enhance the representation and voice of the Global South in international affairs.

In comments, Mendo'o said the Global South, including Africa and China, should participate in the global rule-setting process.

"The Global South is not just a subject to be discussed. The Global South should be part of devising the items, and should be part of actually setting the rules too," he said.

Mendo'o also emphasized that Global South countries should unite as a collective force to address challenges proactively, as individual countries can only progress fast while collective effort enables long-term and far-reaching development.

"One country in the Global South cannot go far," he said. "But together, we can go far."

item.title: Behind the scenes fight for affordable healthcare in the U.S.
item.description: Behind the scenes fight for affordable healthcare in the U.S.
item.content:encoded:
$28,303 - That’s how much the average work-sponsored health insurance plan now costs for a family of four in the United States. And that doesn’t include out of pocket expenses for things like medications, copays or deductibles, which can add thousands of dollars more.  

8 - 15% - That’s how much more expensive health insurance premiums, on average, will be next year. Harvard health economist Meredith Rosenthal tells CGTN that even people making $100,000 a year are feeling squeezed. 

5 million - That’s how many people dropped their health insurance altogether this year after U.S. lawmakers allowed Affordable Care Act subsidies to expire. 

Experts say that rising costs and new eligibility requirements could force another 4 million people to drop their health coverage in 2027. 

Seniors are also feeling squeezed. Their deductibles are rising and more are seeking help to afford medication, treatments and doctor visits. 

The HealthWell Foundation is a nonprofit trying to bridge the gap between healthcare costs and healthcare needs. 

CGTN's Toni Waterman spoke to two employees answering these calls for help.

For more, check out our exclusive content on CGTN Now and subscribe to our weekly newsletter, The China Report.

item.title: Senior Saudi, Pakistani, Turkish officials in Tehran security talks
item.description: High-level delegations from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye were in Tehran on Monday for talks with Iranian authorities aimed at averting renewed fighting between Iran and Israel and the United States, Iran's Foreign Ministry said.
item.content:encoded:
High-level delegations from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye were in Tehran on Monday for talks with Iranian authorities aimed at averting renewed fighting between Iran, Israel and the United States, Iran's Foreign Ministry said.

The delegations were led by Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and Ibrahim Kalin, director of Türkiye's National Intelligence Organization. They were to meet Iran's top security officials and negotiators to push for a deal between Tehran and Washington.

The three countries are signatories to the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement, signed in August, under which an armed attack on any one of them is considered an attack on all.

Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), named the three officials as participants in the meeting, the official IRNA news agency reported. He said Munir announced the decision during talks with SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei on a recent trip to Tehran, and that Rezaei would also attend. The meeting will focus on security issues in the West Asia region, Bagheri Kani said, adding that he hoped participants would work toward establishing an "endogenous" security regime through regional participation.

Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei told reporters that the agenda for the meeting had not been set, but that the talks would "undoubtedly address the most pressing threats to regional security."

Saudi Arabia said in a statement that the delegations hoped to find "ways to de-escalate tensions, enhance regional security and promote its stability."

The war in Yemen and strikes by the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels against Saudi Arabia were also on the table, according to two regional officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The talks come as many in Iran are anxious about a possible return to all-out war. Israeli and American leaders have sharpened their threats ahead of elections in both countries, while Iranian leaders have remained defiant. Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran on Sunday, working in coordination with the United States, as part of ongoing efforts to ease regional tensions, according to a regional official.

(With input from agencies)

item.title: Major trial for new Ebola vaccine begins in DR Congo amid outbreak
item.description: The DRC has launched the Phase 2/3 "Tumaini" clinical trial in Bunia to evaluate candidate vaccines against the Bundibugyo Ebola virus during its largest recorded outbreak. Using a ring vaccination approach for high-risk contacts, the trial aims to evaluate safety and efficacy to combat an epidemic that has claimed over 4,600 lives since May.
item.content:encoded:
A major clinical trial to evaluate vaccines against the Bundibugyo Ebola virus began Friday in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with the first participants vaccinated as the country battles the largest recorded outbreak of the virus.

The Phase 2/3 trial, known as Tumaini, was launched in Bunia, the capital of the hardest-hit Ituri Province, said the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, which is funding and supporting the study.

The trial comes amid a worsening Ebola crisis that has claimed more than 4,600 lives in the DRC since May. Despite the scale of the outbreak, no vaccine has yet been approved specifically against the Bundibugyo virus.

Tumaini, meaning "hope" in Swahili, aims to assess the safety, immune responses and effectiveness of several vaccine candidates, particularly among people who have been in contact with confirmed Ebola patients and face a high risk of infection.

The trial uses an adaptive platform design, allowing multiple vaccine candidates to be evaluated within a single study through a ring vaccination approach targeting contacts of confirmed cases.

The first vaccine entering the trial is Ervebo, which is already licensed to prevent disease caused by the Zaire Ebola virus but has not been proven effective against the Bundibugyo virus.

Two additional vaccines specifically developed against the Bundibugyo virus, one by Moderna and another by the University of Oxford in collaboration with the Serum Institute of India, are expected to join the trial "shortly."

"The launch of the Tumaini trial marks a critical step towards establishing whether candidate vaccines can effectively protect people against the Bundibugyo virus," said Chikwe Ihekweazu, executive director of the World Health Organization's Health Emergencies Program.

WHO Regional Director for Africa Mohamed Janabi also welcomed the launch Friday, saying the trial would generate crucial evidence on candidate vaccines while strengthening the response to the ongoing outbreak and preparedness for future epidemics.

According to the latest figures released late Wednesday by the DRC's health authorities, the country had recorded 9,704 confirmed Ebola cases, including 4,687 deaths, as of October 20, with a case fatality rate of 48.3%.

The epidemic was declared in the DRC on May 15 and designated a public health emergency of international concern by the WHO two days later. The Africa CDC subsequently declared it a public health emergency of continental security.

The current Ebola outbreak has become the largest and deadliest ever recorded in the DRC and the second-largest Ebola outbreak globally, after the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic.

item.title: River dolphins: Uneven conservation gains across the globe
item.description: River dolphins: Uneven conservation gains across the globe
item.content:encoded:
October 24 marks International Freshwater Dolphin Day. 

The observance is not designated by the United Nations. It was proposed at a workshop on establishing protected areas for freshwater cetaceans, held in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, in October 2009, according to the IUCN SSC Cetacean Specialist Group. 

The day aims to raise awareness of freshwater dolphins and their habitats, including the Ganges river dolphin, Indus river dolphin, Amazon river dolphin and the freshwater Yangtze finless porpoise.

Freshwater cetaceans across the globe are under pressure from habitat degradation, fisheries bycatch and other human activities. 

In China, the Yangtze finless porpoise has recorded a population rebound.

A 2025 dedicated survey counted 1,426 individuals, an increase of 177 from the 2022 survey, officials announced at a press conference held by the State Council Information Office on the mid-term assessment of the Yangtze fishing ban on January 30, 2026.

The recovery is linked to the decade-long fishing ban on key Yangtze waterways launched in 2021, alongside protected-area expansion and targeted rescue programs, as stated by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs at the briefing.

This progress contrasts with the fragile status of other river dolphin populations in South and Southeast Asia. The Ganges river dolphin, found in India and Bangladesh, is listed as endangered on the IUCN Red List.

Its main threats include dams and barrages that fragment river habitats, water extraction, industrial and agricultural pollution, and accidental entanglement in fishing nets, per IUCN and WWF assessments.

Freshwater subpopulations of the Irrawaddy dolphin in Indonesia's Mahakam River and Myanmar's Ayeyarwady River are classified as critically endangered by the IUCN SSC Cetacean Specialist Group.

These small, isolated groups are highly vulnerable to gillnet bycatch, vessel strikes and habitat loss.

Local authorities and conservation groups have set up protected zones and rolled out fishing monitoring rules, yet persistent risks slow population recovery.

WWF conservation experts note that river dolphins serve as key biological indicators of river ecosystem health.

While the Yangtze case shows that targeted regulation can reverse declines, many transboundary river systems still lack coordinated cross-border action to safeguard remaining freshwater dolphin habitats in Asia and South America.

item.title: Canadian scholar: China-proposed GGI offers multipolar order of peace
item.description: The China-proposed Global Governance Initiative (GGI), launched one year ago at a time of "great chaos" in the world, reinforces China's resolve to act as a force of peace and invites all countries to build a multipolar world order that puts people at its heart, a Canadian scholar said.
item.content:encoded:
The China-proposed Global Governance Initiative (GGI), launched one year ago at a time of "great chaos" in the world, reinforces China's resolve to act as a force of peace and invites all countries to build a multipolar world order that puts people at its heart, a Canadian scholar said.

"The Global Governance Initiative has further underlined China's intention of continuing to serve as an oasis of peace, of expanding that zone of peace beyond China's borders to include more and more countries," Radhika Desai, director of the Geopolitical Economy Research Group at the University of Manitoba in Canada, told CGTN in an interview on Sunday.

Desai described the GGI as an open invitation for the international community to jointly build a "cooperative, multilateral, rules-based, and multipolar" world order that is "aimed at producing people-centered development."

Central to the Chinese initiative is respect for every country's economic sovereignty, granting nations the right to shape their own economic arrangements to fit their development needs and the interests of their people, she added.

The Canadian professor of political studies was among nearly 400 representatives from strategic, political, academic, business, media, and youth sectors from more than 90 countries and international and regional organizations, including the United Nations, who attended the three-day 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan) that concluded on Sunday.

Hosted by the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs, it is themed "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World."

(Cover: Radhika Desai, director of the Geopolitical Economy Research Group at the University of Manitoba in Canada, during the interview with CGTN at Forum in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province, October 25, 2026. /CGTN)

item.title: Xiongan's underground backbone: The tech inside a 'city of the future'
item.description: Xiongan's underground backbone: The tech inside a 'city of the future'
item.content:encoded:
Where many cities lay underground utilities without an integrated monitoring backbone, Xiongan has built a connected nervous system befitting China's "city of the future."

The startup hub in Hebei plays host to the 2026 Global Governance Forum from October 23-25, giving delegates a window into its "three-city" development vision: the city underground, the city aboveground and the city in the cloud.

Planners flipped the script from first principles: "Build underground first, above ground second." Unlike conventional cities, where utilities are laid separately, Xiongan routes water, power, telecom and heating through an integrated network of shared utility tunnels. 

Figures were released at an official Xiongan press conference in December 2025, showing more than 1,000 kilometers of pipelines run inside these corridors, a layout designed to eliminate chronic road excavation.

The 106-km tunnel network, running steadily for over 1,500 days by late 2025, operates as a living digital twin. 

BIM-based models and digital sensors monitor water pressure, temperature, humidity and gas levels, feeding real-time data into a central control system.

Robots do the legwork. 

State Grid Xiongan Power Supply Company engineer Wei Ziren notes that an 11.75 km stretch in the Zagang area – once a grueling 22-hour job for two human inspectors – is now swept by five Xiongan Lingxi quadruped robots in three to four hours.

Underground hardware feeds straight into the urban management platform. A "Beidou + 5G" indoor positioning system extends satellite navigation below ground to deliver parking-level precision in the Rongdong area, according to the Xiongan Aerospace Information Research Institute. 

Automated smart cameras flag standing water above 10 centimeters instantly. Integrated with the Baiyangdian watershed and designed to withstand a 50-year flood standard in the zone, the infrastructure reduces water runoff pressure while keeping spare capacity wide open for future upgrades, so roads will not need to be repeatedly torn up.

item.title: Kenya records second Ebola death as outbreak reaches nine cases
item.description: The latest victim, a 65-year-old woman and close relative of the first patient, died on Friday while receiving treatment.
item.content:encoded:
Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola, with nine confirmed cases reported in the country, according to the Ministry of Health.

The latest victim, a 65-year-old woman and close relative of the first patient, died on Friday while receiving treatment. She developed symptoms on October 13 while in quarantine, the ministry said.

Seven other patients are receiving treatment at two isolation facilities. All eight secondary cases are linked to the first imported case, and authorities say there is no evidence of wider community transmission. 

The first patient, a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), travelled to Nairobi via Uganda on October 3. He died on October 5 after receiving treatment at several hospitals in the DRC and was later given a safe and dignified burial.

Kenya has strengthened screening at points of entry, including for travellers arriving from the DRC, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, Zambia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and the Central African Republic. Travellers from these countries are required to complete health declaration forms to support screening and contact tracing. 

Authorities continue to use quarantine, patient isolation, contact tracing and enhanced border screening to limit further transmission.

(With input from wires)

item.title: Macron calls for halt to demonstrations in coming days
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that the government recommends that no demonstrations be held across the country in the coming days, particularly on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that the government recommends that no demonstrations be held across the country in the coming days, particularly on Saturday.

Speaking after a security council meeting, Macron said the government intended to prohibit requests to organize gatherings by people "who have no legitimacy to do so." For trade union marches formally notified to local authorities, alternative routes would be proposed to protect city centers, he added.

The prefecture of the Rhone department has banned all demonstrations in Lyon for Saturday, French television channel BFM TV reported.

In Toulon, a city in southern France, authorities have banned demonstrations in the city center from 11 a.m. (1000 GMT) to 11:59 p.m. (2259 GMT) on Saturday. A temporary curfew for unaccompanied minors will also be in force in the city center from 6 p.m. (1700 GMT) on Saturday to 6 a.m. (0400 GMT) on Sunday, according to BFM TV.

In Nice, southeastern France, the prefect of the Alpes-Maritimes department has banned all gatherings, marches and protest demonstrations in the city center from 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) to midnight (2200 GMT) on Saturday, citing risks to public order and violence.

In Paris, a demonstration scheduled for Saturday between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Nation, organized notably at the initiative of the General Confederation of Labour (CGT), will be allowed to proceed, the Paris police prefecture said on Thursday.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Tuesday that the government would deploy soldiers from the French army's Operation Sentinelle to help prevent violence during the demonstrations announced for October 24.

item.description: China, Djibouti issue communiqué on Horn of Africa, Red Sea security
item.content:encoded:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Djibouti's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulkader Houssein Omar in Beijing on Wednesday. 

The two ministers discussed bilateral relations and issues of common concern, with Wang saying that bilateral relations continue to maintain healthy and stable momentum. He noted that political mutual trust has deepened and that cooperation across various fields has brought benefits to the people of Djibouti. Omar said that Djibouti is willing to further enrich the connotation of the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries.

The two sides issued a joint press communiqué on safeguarding peace and stability in the Horn of Africa and the security of shipping lanes in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Wang said the communiqué aims to send a unified message to the international community, demonstrates a shared commitment to promoting regional stability and reflects the common aspirations of African and Arab countries.

The two sides also signed a memorandum of understanding on jointly advancing cooperation under the Global Security Initiative.

item.title: Israeli operation displaces over 2,600 in West Bank's Hebron
item.description: Israeli forces have pressed ahead with a military operation and a lockdown in the Hebron area of the occupied West Bank since Friday, demolishing and destroying a number of Palestinian civilian and commercial facilities and causing heavy property losses, Palestinian officials said on Sunday. Hundreds of Palestinian families have been affected, with more than 2,000 civilians directly impacted.
item.content:encoded:
Israeli forces have pressed ahead with a military operation and a lockdown in the Hebron area of the occupied West Bank since Friday, demolishing and destroying a number of Palestinian civilian and commercial facilities and causing heavy property losses, Palestinian officials said on Sunday. Hundreds of Palestinian families have been affected, with more than 2,000 civilians directly impacted.

The office of the Palestinian prime minister said that, citing data from the Hebron governorate, more than 2,670 Palestinians have been forcibly expelled from their homes in Hebron by Israeli forces, most of them women, children and elderly people. Some residents were beaten by Israeli soldiers when they tried to return home.

Apart from demolishing homes and expelling residents, Israeli forces have also intensively installed roadblocks and sealed iron gates, cutting off main roads and seriously disrupting local supply chains and the movement of people. Israeli settlers have also levelled land belonging to Palestinian residents in the southern Hebron area and pitched tents, in preparation for setting up an outpost for an Israeli settlement.

The Hebron governorate announced on Sunday that several cities in the area would set up joint emergency operations rooms running 24 hours a day, using all available municipal resources to help residents affected by the operation. It is also stepping up work on a legal document to be formally submitted to the International Criminal Court.

Palestinian officials also reported incidents elsewhere in the occupied West Bank of Israeli forces destroying Palestinian civilian property and Israeli settlers carrying out attacks. In a Palestinian village west of Ramallah, Israeli forces used heavy machinery to level large tracts of land and forcibly uprooted dozens of olive trees in the middle of the harvest season, for the construction of a road unilaterally planned by Israel leading to a nearby Israeli settlement. In a Palestinian village near Nablus, Israeli settlers attacked and detained several Palestinian civilians picking olives and forcibly transferred them into a nearby Israeli settlement.

item.title: Meet the APEC economies: Chile
item.description: Meet the APEC economies: Chile
item.content:encoded:
From copper to cherries, Chile's exports reach markets across the Asia-Pacific. 

In 2024, a total of 5,410 Chilean companies exported to APEC economies, supporting more than 917,000 direct, formal jobs, according to Chile's trade authorities. 

Half of those exporters were micro, small and medium-sized businesses.

item.title: China congratulates Lula on his presidential election victory
item.description: China on Monday congratulated Brazilian incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his victory in the country's presidential runoff, pledging to work with Brazil to further advance the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future.
item.content:encoded:
China has noted that Brazil's Superior Electoral Court announced President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's victory in the second round of Brazil's presidential election, and extends its congratulations, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular press briefing on Monday.

China stands ready to work with Brazil to steadily advance the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future, Guo added

item.title: Wang Huning accompanies DPRK top leader on visit to border city
item.description: China's top political advisor Wang Huning on Saturday accompanied Kim Jong Un, general secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and president of the State Affairs of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), on a visit to Dandong in northeast China's Liaoning Province.
item.content:encoded:
China's top political advisor Wang Huning on Saturday accompanied Kim Jong Un, general secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and president of the State Affairs of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), on a visit to Dandong in northeast China's Liaoning Province.

Wang, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, conveyed General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping's cordial greetings and best wishes to Kim.

On Saturday morning, Wang greeted Kim at the square of the Memorial Hall of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea and accompanied him to present a flower basket to the memorial tower.

The national anthems of China and the DPRK were played, and honor guards laid the flower basket. Kim approached the flower basket and arranged the ribbon, which read, "The martyrs of the Chinese People's Volunteers (CPV) are always remembered." In a solemn atmosphere, all present paid silent tribute to the martyrs.

Inside the memorial hall, Kim viewed the historical artifacts showcasing the bravery of the martyrs and the side-by-side fighting of Chinese and DPRK soldiers and gifted a historical photo bearing his personal inscription to the hall.

During their meeting, Wang said on the occasion of the 76th anniversary of the CPV's entry into the DPRK to fight in the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, General Secretary Kim Jong Un's special trip to Dandong fully demonstrates how much the party and government of the DPRK value the China-DPRK friendship forged with blood.

He said the visit is highly significant, as it not only carries forward the traditional friendship between China and the DPRK and consolidates the popular support for friendship but also deepens political mutual trust and advances cooperation and development.

In September last year and June this year, General Secretary Xi Jinping and General Secretary Kim Jong Un made historic mutual visits and reached a series of important common understandings, guiding the traditional friendly and cooperative relations between China and the DPRK into a new historical period, Wang said.

China stands ready to work with the DPRK to unswervingly implement the important consensus reached between the top leaders of the two parties and two countries and take their common socialist cause as a bond to further develop China-DPRK relations, Wang said.

The opening of the new China-DPRK Yalu River bridge can be taken as an opportunity to expand personnel exchanges and trade cooperation and better benefit the two peoples, he said.

He called for strengthening strategic communication and collaboration to foster a peaceful and stable external environment for safeguarding their respective sovereignty, security and development.
