item.title: Jordan tightens security after deadly church attack kills eight
item.description: Jordan tightens security after deadly church attack kills eight
item.content:encoded:
Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan, the US embassy in Amman said on Saturday, as authorities searched for gunmen who killed eight people and wounded 40 in a church attack.

The assailants fired for several minutes in broad daylight during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate on Friday, in what Jordanian authorities described as an act of extremist terrorism. There was no immediate claim of responsibility.

Such attacks are rare in Jordan, although authorities in the US-allied kingdom say they have repeatedly foiled plots by Islamist militants in recent years.

Authorities said they were still searching for the attackers, adding that it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan.

"A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word," said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated. A relative of Ammarin's was injured in the attack.

Reuters video footage showed police patrolling outside the Hamoud church on Saturday, about 120 kilometers southwest of the capital, Amman.

"This is a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism, and we will not allow society to go down this path," Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said in a post on X.

Jordan's King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against militant Islamist groups, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist."

Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world.

Jordan has been among the US allies in the Middle East hit by Iranian attacks this year, after the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.

item.title: Bolsonaro allies recognize Lula's victory despite election challenge
item.description: Several Brazilian political parties and figures that backed Flavio Bolsonaro in Sunday's presidential runoff have recognized incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection, distancing themselves from Bolsonaro's bid to annul the vote.
item.content:encoded:
Several Brazilian political parties and figures that backed Flavio Bolsonaro in Sunday's presidential runoff have recognized incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection, distancing themselves from Bolsonaro's bid to annul the vote.

Lula received 51.79% of valid votes in the runoff, against 48.21% for Bolsonaro, according to results released by Brazil's Superior Electoral Court on Sunday night.

On Sunday night, Bolsonaro announced that he would seek to have the election annulled after Supreme Federal Court Justice Cristiano Zanin extended voting by two hours following reports of transportation problems and heavy rains that affected voters in some cities.

Despite Bolsonaro's challenge, the Brazilian Democratic Movement (MDB), Uniao Brasil and Republicanos president Marcos Pereira congratulated Lula on his victory.

Pereira called for respect for political differences and dialogue with Congress, saying the new term carried a responsibility to govern for all Brazilians, including those who voted for Bolsonaro.

MDB, chaired by re-elected Congressman Baleia Rossi, also recognized the result. In a post on X, the party said Sunday that Lula was democratically re-elected in accordance with the country's 1988 Constitution and described the result as an expression of the sovereign will of the people.

Uniao Brasil, which backed Bolsonaro in the runoff, said Monday that the will of the people, freely expressed at the ballot box, must be respected.

The Progressive Party (PP), which also supported Bolsonaro, had not issued an official statement as of Monday morning. However, Senator-elect Arthur Lira, a PP member and former speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, acknowledged the election result and called for dialogue and responsibility.

item.title: Iran reports tanker blasts in Hormuz as Trump hints at renewed strikes
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said two supertankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, as regional countries called for the waterway to reopen and US President Donald Trump signaled the possibility of renewed military action against Iran.
item.content:encoded:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said two supertankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, as regional countries called for the waterway to reopen and US President Donald Trump signaled the possibility of renewed military action against Iran.

The IRGC Navy said that two supertankers seeking to cross the "unauthorized" route south of the Strait of Hormuz suffered explosions after hitting naval mines.

The blasts set the vessels' engine rooms on fire, bringing them to a halt, the navy said in a statement published on the IRGC's official news outlet Sepah News.

Earlier in the day, the semi-official Tasnim news agency quoted a source close to the IRGC Navy as saying that traffic by "violating" vessels in the Strait of Hormuz had been "completely stopped" after Iran destroyed navigational aid systems serving such ships and targeted four "offending" tankers in the waterway on Thursday.

The reported incidents come amid growing concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the region. Greece-based consultancy Marisks told Reuters that "October 2026 has emerged as the most intense period of maritime attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the escalation of hostilities in March."

UKMTO, the British maritime security service, which recorded 135 incidents related to the US-Iran conflict as of October 16, also reported a sharp rise in ship damage caused by attacks in October.

Regional, European countries call for reopening of Hormuz

Also on Friday, foreign ministers from eight regional and European countries met in Istanbul, calling for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

The meeting brought together four regional countries – Türkiye, Egypt, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia – and four European nations – Britain, France, Germany and Italy.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan told reporters that all participants shared a common understanding on the need for dialogue to prevent the destruction from spreading further.

The meeting underscored growing diplomatic efforts to address the risks posed by disruptions to shipping through the strait, as tensions between Washington and Tehran continue.

Could the US launch another military operation against Iran?

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump on Friday raised the prospect of renewed military strikes against Iran, claiming that the United States could seize all of the country's oil or even take over the entire country. "Iran is not able to do much now. And we could, if we wanted to, just take all of the oil," Trump told reporters as he left the White House for a rally in Florida. "We could take the whole country."

Asked about US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz saying the conflict with Iran could drag on for another year, Trump said: "We could end it very quickly. The question is, 'Do we want to finish it off or do we just want to let it wither?'"

Later at the Florida rally, Trump suggested another military operation against Iran was possible. "We may do another little Epic Fury," he told attendees, referring to the large-scale US military operation against Iran launched on February 28 alongside a coordinated Israeli offensive.

Trump's latest remarks came amid reports that the US and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the US midterm elections. However, whether Trump will ultimately authorize another military operation remains uncertain, according to US media reports.

Also on Wednesday, Iran warned regional countries that any support for the United States in the event of renewed hostilities would be regarded as a hostile act against Tehran.

Li Zixin, a Middle East expert at the China Institute of International Studies, told China Media Group that avoiding military action before the US midterm elections has become the White House's publicly stated position. "The reason is straightforward: a war would drive up oil prices and inflation, while Trump needs to keep oil prices down ahead of the elections," Li said.

For now, the most likely scenario is continued stalemate, with localized clashes persisting, Li said, adding that after the elections, both military action and negotiations could enter a new window of opportunity for change.

After the midterm elections, with fewer political constraints, the US military could maintain its blockade of Iran while remaining prepared for potential large-scale military operations against the country, leaving open the option of sustained strikes, Li said.

(With input from agencies)

item.title: China-Europe freight train trips on eastern corridor hit record high
item.description: The number of China-Europe freight train trips through the network's eastern corridor reached a record high so far this year, while the range of goods transported has increasingly shifted toward higher-value, technology-intensive products.
item.content:encoded:
The number of China-Europe freight train trips through the network's eastern corridor reached a record high so far this year, while the range of goods transported has increasingly shifted toward higher-value, technology-intensive products.

As of Friday, the corridor had handled 6,024 trips this year, up 40.3% year on year, marking the first time annual traffic through the corridor has surpassed 6,000 trips.

The corridor comprises three major railway ports in Manzhouli, Suifenhe and Tongjiang, connecting more than 60 Chinese cities with 14 European countries.

In the first three quarters of this year, the Shijiazhuang International Land Port in north China's Hebei Province operated 1,023 China-Europe freight trains and handled 103,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) of import and export containers, according to Shijiazhuang Customs. The figures increased 27.4% and 26%, respectively, year on year, both reaching record highs for the same period.

As a major China-Europe freight train hub in northern China, the Shijiazhuang port now operates 27 regular routes that connect more than 50 countries and regions across Asia and Europe.

The port's cargo mix has also evolved from daily consumer goods and textile materials to higher-value products, including electronics, photovoltaic products and high-end equipment, reflecting the growing role of technology-intensive and higher-value goods in China's exports.

Meanwhile, Shanghai's foreign trade also reached a record high in the first three quarters. According to Shanghai Customs, the city's ports handled 10.35 trillion yuan ($1.5 trillion) worth of imports and exports during the period, up 23.7% year on year.

The figure accounted for 25.9% of China's total foreign trade, keeping Shanghai's ports in the top spot nationwide.
